prompt: Some people believe that it is parents who teach children to recycle waste. While others feel schools are more responsible. Discuss both views. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay:
Recycling has become an essential habit in modern society as environmental problems continue to grow. While some people argue that mothers and fathers should take primary responsibility for teaching the younger generation to recycle, others believe that educational institutions are in a better position to provide this education. This essay will discuss both viewpoints before explaining why I believe that the family plays a more important role, although schools also make a valuable contribution.

On the one hand, many people think the family is mainly responsible because young people develop their earliest habits at home. They spend most of their time with their families, observing and copying adult behaviour. If adults regularly separate plastic, paper, and food waste, youngsters are likely to adopt these practices naturally. Moreover, caregivers can explain why recycling is important during everyday activities, such as shopping or throwing away rubbish. As a result, environmental responsibility becomes part of a child's daily routine rather than just a school subject.

On the other hand, educational institutions also have a significant role in promoting recycling awareness. Teachers can provide scientific knowledge about environmental issues and organise practical activities, such as recycling projects or campus clean-up campaigns. These experiences help pupils understand the long-term consequences of waste pollution and encourage teamwork. In addition, schools can ensure that every learner receives the same environmental education, even if recycling is not practised at home.

In my opinion, although educational institutions provide worthwhile knowledge and opportunities, the greater duty falls to families because they shape young people's behaviour from an early age. Good habits are formed through daily repetition, and this happens primarily in the home environment. However, the most effective approach is for families and schools to work together so that young people receive consistent messages both at home and in the classroom.

In conclusion, both families and schools play significant roles in teaching the younger generation to recycle. Nevertheless, I believe parents are more accountable because they influence their children's attitudes and habits during their formative years, while teachers reinforce these lessons through education and practical experience.
